Asif S/o Jamaluddin R/o H.No.101, Block-H Lal Kuan, New Delhi. Also at: H.No.188, Mohalla-Badbaliyan PS-Bithore, Tehsil-Mawana Distt-Meerut, U.P. ............Driver-cum-owner/Respondent no.1 2. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Kanchenjunga Building, 18, floor No.8, Barakhamba Road Delhi. Also at: 1770-A-4/8, Kalkaji Govindpuri, Delhi-110019. ...........Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Charu by Charu Gupta Gupta 2025.08.19 Date: 17:29:01 +0530 Mact No:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 1 Of 18 Bk Date of accident : 03.01.2016 Result of accident : Injury Date of filing of Petition : 02.11.2018 Date of Decision : 19.08.2025 Award 1 . The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Gulfam suffered grievous injury and sustained fracture in his left pelvis.
texts.facts: 1 . The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Gulfam suffered grievous injury and sustained fracture in his left pelvis. An application u/s 166(1) MV Gulfam vs Md. Asif on 19 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134791303/ 1 Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/petitioner. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 03.01.2016, petitioner was driving his car bearing no.DL-9CM-9274 from Bijnaur to Delhi at a normal speed on the correct side of the road. At about 11 am, when the car reached near Pulia/Bridge of Samaspur, PS Behasuma, Meerut, U.P., another car bearing no.DL-8CJ-6938 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came driven in a rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and dashed into the car which petitioner was driving. Due to the accident, petitioner sustained injuries and was rushed to Mawana hospital from where he was referred to Govt. hospital, Meerut and thereafter to JPN Apex Trauma Center. 3. An FIR no.005/2016, dated 13.01.2016 was registered u/s 279/337/338/427 of IPC at PS Behsuma, Distt-Meerut, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver-cum-owner and respondent no.2 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.08.19 17:29:09 +0530 MACT NO:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 2 Of 18 BK was insured. 5. Respondent no.1 filed his reply denying involvement of the vehicle in the accident and negligence on his part. He stated that his vehicle was duly insured/ Respondent no.2 from 02.01.2016 to 01.01.2017 vide policy no. 2002053115P111893469. In its reply, respondent no.2 has refuted its liability denying the occurrence of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and alleged sole negligence of the petitioner who was driving vehicle no.DL-9CM-9274. 6. Vide order dated 30.11.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured Gulfam suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 03.01.2016 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-8CJ-6938 driven and owned by R1 and insured with R2? 7. Despite opportunity, petitioner did not lead any evidence. No evidence was either led by the respondents. Vide order dated 30.11.2019, the interest of the petitioner was also directed to be closed from such date till completion of their evidence, unless advance copy of the affidavit with Gulfam vs Md. Asif on 19 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134791303/ 2 documents and list of witnesses was supplied to the respondents. Since the order was not complied and the petitioner neither filed any list of witnesses nor supplied advance copy of his evidence, the interest of the petitioner is deemed closed with effect from 30.11.2019. The CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.19 17:29:16 +0530 MACT NO:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 3 Of 18 BK petitioner shall thus not be entitled to interest from 30.11.2019. 8. At the same time, since the proceedings before MACT are in the nature of inquiry proceedings, the documents filed alongwith the petitioner and reply may be considered for adjudicating the claim. Reliance is placed on decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. v. Jaibir Singh & Ors.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 14. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 15. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) CHARU GUPTA Date: GUPTA 2025.08.19 17:29:43 +0530 MACT NO:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 7 Of 18 BK (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). 15.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the Gulfam vs Md. Asif on 19 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134791303/ 5 heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 15.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.19 17:29:50 +0530 MACT NO:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 8 Of 18 BK evidence. 15.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 15.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 15.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 15.7. 24. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.19 17:30:49 +0530 MACT NO:1020/18 Gulfam v. Md. ASif P.No. 14 Of 18 BK beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". They are taking such a rigid and mechanical approach without understanding and appreciating the distinction drawn by this Court in the case of minors, illiterate claimants and Gulfam vs Md. Asif on 19 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134791303/ 10 widows and in the case of semiliterate and literate persons.
